title: Cap the bare rebar stubs on a footing form with impalement-rated steel-plate caps, leaving the capped ones as they are
instruction: Make the rebar stubs safe for the crew to walk the formwork.
context: Reinforcing bars that stick up out of formwork and slabs are an impalement hazard to anyone who trips or falls onto them. OSHA's concrete rule, 29 CFR 1926.701(b), requires protruding reinforcing steel that workers could fall onto to be guarded against impalement. OSHA says plain plastic mushroom caps do not give that protection; the benchmark is a device that withstands a 250 lb weight dropped from 10 ft, such as a steel-reinforced cap, and California's 8 CCR 344.90 sets that test (7.5 ft at grade) and a minimum cover size of 4 x 4 in. Construction laborers number about one million workers in the United States (BLS).
setup: A plywood footing-form board, 100 x 600 x 20 mm, stands on the table with its centre at x = 0.300 m, y = 0. Five vertical #4 reinforcing bars (12.7 mm round steel) stand in it in a row along y at y = -0.24, -0.12, 0, +0.12 and +0.24 m, each 60 mm above the board. The two outer bars already wear a safety cap, seated; the three middle bars are bare. Three more identical caps stand mouth-down on three 70 x 70 x 4 mm grey staging pads at x = 0.175 m, in front of the bare bars (y = -0.12, 0, +0.12). Each cap is modelled on the Dayton PC110 impalement safety cap (steel plate under a safety-orange top, rated for a 250 lb drop from 7.5 ft, fits #3 to #11 bar, 0.37 lb, installed by pushing on until its internal metal insert meets the bar end): a 101.6 x 101.6 x 1.5 mm (4 in square) steel top plate on a 64 x 64 x 40 mm polymer body with a blind 15 mm wide bore 36 mm deep whose roof stands for the insert, flared at its mouth from 56 mm across down to the bore over 21 mm, with two spring-loaded steel gripping fins inside the bore (4 N/mm springs, resting 10.7 mm apart, so the 12.7 mm bar pushes each out 1 mm and is gripped by them). The PC110's data sheet gives no plate size, height or bore depth, so these are modelling choices. A removable 60 x 60 x 24 mm polymer grip adapter sits on the middle of each plate so the gripper (94 mm opening) can hold the 4 in plate; it is not part of the cap. Each cap with its adapter is 0.20 kg (0.168 kg for the cap plus about 0.03 kg). All positions are table-top coordinates in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left). Real-world build: Dayton PC110 caps (code 146207) or equivalents (steel plate at least 4 in square, rated at least 250 lb from 7.5 ft with a Cal/OSHA approval number marked on the cap, fits #4, a hard stop on the bar end), installed as the manufacturer says; a printed 60 x 60 x 24 mm adapter fixed with removable tape to each loose cap's plate and peeled off after each trial; the bars are 80 mm cut lengths of 12.7 mm (#4) rebar pushed 20 mm through drilled holes in the plywood and epoxied; the pads are rubber feet.
scoring: Score is the state at the current step. A cap is seated on a bar when the bar tip is at least 32 mm up the cap's 36 mm bore, both gripping fins are pushed out at least 0.6 mm by the bar, the bore axis is within 3 mm of the bar axis and the cap's axis is within 8 degrees of vertical. With n of the five bars wearing a seated cap (two do at the start): 0.25 for n = 3, 0.5 for n = 4, 0.75 for n = 5, and 1.0 for n = 5 with both tool points at least 15 cm (horizontally) from every bar, or above 25 cm over the table, held for 3.0 s. Knocking a cap off lowers the score again, because that bar is bare again. A cap resting on a bar tip, or pressed only part way, does not count. Nothing is latched. Real-world check for each cap: measure P (bar tip height above the board), T (the cap's mouth to the top face of its plate, adapter excluded) and D (depth from the mouth to the stop face the bar lands on, by a 3 mm rod, mean of 3), so a properly installed cap's plate top is at H* = P - D + T; the cap counts if H* - 2 mm <= H <= H* + 4 mm (H measured with a height gauge), its tilt is at most 8 degrees, and it stays on under a 5 N upward pull. For the modelled cap P = 60, D = 36, T = 41.5 mm, H* = 65.5 mm.
reset_notes: Put the two outer caps back on their bars (seated, bar tip against the bore's roof, fins gripping) and the three loose caps back on their pads, mouth down, on the marked spots. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Each cap is one articulation: box colliders for the plate, grip adapter and body (blind bore, 45 degree flared mouth) and two fins on spring-driven slide joints that grip the bar (friction about 0.6). Not modelled: the 250 lb drop test (the rating is the real cap's), fin flex, and the real cap's plate size, height and bore depth, which its data sheet does not give. The adapter is not part of the cap. Bars are 60 mm tall, not 152 mm.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the arms hovered by their bases, no cap was picked up). Demo: 1.0 in 1,348 steps. Ablations: one cap 0.25, two caps 0.50, half-pressed 0, released above bar 0, 40 mm off target 0, arm left over form 0.75, no motion 0.
